title: Real quantifier alternation versus summation
formal: For every fixed \(t\ge1\), does the truth problem for closed real-arithmetic sentences with at most \(t\) alternating quantifier blocks admit a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction to \(\Sigma\text{-}\mathrm{ETR}\), the existential theory of the reals with Boolean summation binders? Equivalently, is every fixed level of the real polynomial hierarchy contained in \(\exists\mathbb R^\Sigma\) as defined below? The polynomial-time reduction and its degree may depend on \(t\); the number of real variables in each block is unrestricted. Either existential or universal first blocks are included.
why: Alternating real quantifiers express geometric and optimization conditions beyond pure existence. Finite summation over Boolean choices adds a form of counting without introducing new real quantifier blocks. Comparing these resources would clarify whether a single strengthened existential theory captures all fixed levels of the real hierarchy.
status_note: Open in the checked ISAAC 2024 Section 9 and its full preprint. The earlier Basu–Zell topological theorem has a different target, while later corrections to bounded-domain real hierarchies do not prove this unrestricted summation containment. Bounded subsequent-result checks through 2026-09-16 verified no resolution.

progress.text: Basu and Zell publish a real Toda analogue based on topological counting. Its oracle is not the summation-only existential theory in this card.
The ISAAC paper defines the summation-only class, proves its PSPACE upper bound, and asks in Section 9 whether it contains the fixed real-alternation levels.
Schaefer–Štefankovič arXiv v6 repairs and limits earlier bounded-domain claims. It retains the unrestricted real hierarchy used here.

category_assignment.reason: The question compares real-algebraic complexity classes and counting power.

importance.reason: The question asks whether a counting-like arithmetic extension can absorb all fixed levels of real quantifier alternation. It would organize a broad hierarchy of real-feasibility and geometric decision problems and distinguish the power of Boolean summation from the stronger succinct and product extensions.
importance.basis: Individual recovery of ISAAC 2024 Section 9, exact operator definitions and the real hierarchy, including the 2025 correction to related bounded-domain claims.

sentences: The question asks whether all fixed levels of alternating real quantification reduce to one strengthened existential theory.
That target theory permits nested sums over Boolean dummy variables inside arithmetic terms.
Its real variables must remain explicitly listed, and it has no compact product binder.
The reductions operate on finite binary descriptions and may have a different polynomial bound for each fixed alternation level.
A positive answer would supply the specific counting-versus-alternation principle proposed in the 2024 source, distinct from earlier topological Toda analogues.

definitions:
The source input is a closed prenex sentence \(Q_1X_1\cdots Q_sX_s\,\phi\), where \(0\le s\le t\), each \(X_j\) is a finite tuple of distinct real variables, consecutive \(Q_j\in\{\exists,\forall\}\) differ, and every quantified variable ranges over all of \(\mathbb R\). There are no free variables. The matrix \(\phi\) is a finite Boolean formula using \(\land,\lor,\neg\) and comparisons \(u=v\), \(u<v\), or \(u\le v\). Its arithmetic terms are finite expression trees built from integer constants, variables, binary addition, subtraction and multiplication. Integers are encoded by a sign and ordinary binary magnitude; variable indices are binary integers. Fix a parenthesized prefix encoding over a finite alphabet for all tree nodes, operators, variable indices and tuple lists. Input size is the full bit length of this encoding. There is no shared-subexpression circuit, implicit large power, summation binder or succinct indexing in these source terms. Binary integer constants and subtraction can equivalently be expressed using the source papers’ constants \(0,1\) and ring operations with polynomial overhead.

A target \(\Sigma\text{-}\mathrm{ETR}\) instance is a closed sentence \(\exists y_1\cdots\exists y_m\,\psi\), where \(m\ge0\), \(\psi\) is a Boolean formula of the same comparisons, and its arithmetic expression trees additionally allow the binder \(\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}u\). This denotes \(u[b:=0]+u[b:=1]\). The bound symbol \(b\) is a local dummy scalar variable, distinct from the existentially quantified real variables and from other active dummy variables; usual capture-free substitution fixes its semantics. Binders may be nested, and their body is stored once, so nesting can describe exponentially many summands. All free variables in terms must be among the explicitly listed \(y_j\) or in scope of a summation binder. A dummy value may occur as a number in a term but cannot select a variable name: an expression such as \(y_b\), with a value-dependent index, is forbidden. No product binder, Boolean-formula binder, arbitrary real constant, real exponentiation, extra real quantifier alternation or succinct circuit representation is allowed. The size counts the finite syntax including each binder and its body, rather than the fully expanded sum. Thus the number of distinct existential real variables is at most the target length.

A deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction is a single finite-program multitape Turing machine that, on each valid input string of length \(L\), outputs one valid target sentence within \(C_t(L+1)^{c_t}\) bit transitions and preserves truth in both directions. It uses no random bits, advice, real-arithmetic oracle or decision oracle. Output length and all construction work count. Constants \(C_t,c_t\) and the machine may depend on the fixed block bound \(t\), but not on a particular input. The target class \(\exists\mathbb R^\Sigma\) consists of binary-string languages polynomial-time many-one reducible to truth of these target sentences. The real polynomial hierarchy here is the union of the analogous closures of the source truth problems over all fixed \(t\). Its definition does not allow the block bound to grow with the input length.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof providing a truth-preserving polynomial-time reduction for every fixed block bound \(t\), or a complete Lean proof that such a reduction fails for at least one fixed \(t\). The affirmative proof must respect the target’s explicit variable list and summation-only syntax. A PSPACE upper bound, a reduction to a language with product binders or exponentially indexed real variables, or a reduction to a topological counting oracle is insufficient by itself.

context_blocks.text: The source’s phrase “real version of Toda’s theorem” is followed by the precise question of containment in \(\exists\mathbb R^\Sigma\). This card uses that containment as its sole target. It does not ask for an unspecified analogue among other real-computation models.

The crucial target restriction is the absence of value-dependent variable indexing. The source distinguishes ordinary \(\Sigma\)-ETR from a stronger summation language capable of addressing exponentially many real variables.

The source proves that the summation class lies in PSPACE and contains ordinary existential real feasibility. By contrast, adding the corresponding compact product binder yields PSPACE-completeness. These bounds do not settle whether summation alone contains all fixed alternation levels.

Schaefer and Štefankovič define the discrete real hierarchy through truth of finitely encoded sentences and polynomial-time reductions. Their March 2025 revision corrects certain bounded-closed-domain claims. The present target uses unrestricted real domains and the full comparison signature, so it does not rely on the withdrawn bounded-domain equivalences.

Basu and Zell already proved a real analogue of Toda’s theorem using topological counting, namely Betti-number information, in a compact real-machine setting. That established theorem has a different oracle and model from the summation-only containment posed in 2024.
